findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Name the specific document, for example "The most recent version of the reimbursement log supersedes the one before it."
findings.location: Program Overview, second paragraph, final sentence
findings.violation: The paragraph mentions two different documents, the equipment catalog and the reimbursement log, and this sentence never says which one has a "most recent version," so the referent is ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing"
findings.fix: Rewrite in chronological order, for example "After the manager signs the request and finance confirms the budget line, the request moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The clause order buries the actual sequence of events, so a reader cannot tell whether the manager signs before or after finance confirms the budget line.

findings.evidence: "the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request"
findings.fix: Clarify whether the confirmation summary is a pre-submission preview or the post-processing confirmation email, and reorder the paragraphs to match the actual sequence.
findings.violation: This sentence places the confirmation review before final submission, but the previous paragraph says the confirmation email arrives only once processing finishes, which is the last step in the sequence. The two paragraphs describe conflicting orders of events.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific request types or dollar thresholds that require more than a photo of the receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" does not say which requests need more than a photo, leaving the reader unable to determine when additional documentation is required.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in the third person used throughout the rest of the document, for example "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This is the only sentence in the document written in second person, "you" and "we." Every other section refers to employees, the employee, and the finance office in third person, so the voice shift reads as inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Pick one term and use it consistently across all three sentences, or explicitly define how the terms relate to each other.
findings.violation: Three consecutive sentences use three different terms, "stipend item," "reimbursable item," and "covered purchase amount," for what appears to be the same thing, without ever stating they are synonyms. A reader cannot tell if these are the same object or three different ones.

findings.evidence: "Countersign the employee request within two business days."
findings.fix: Add the subject, for example "The manager countersigns the employee request within two business days."
findings.violation: This sentence has no subject, so it is unclear who is supposed to countersign the request.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a complete, parallel list, for example "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt," and add the remaining steps the heading implies.
findings.violation: The sentence is grammatically incomplete. "The uploaded receipt" is a noun phrase that does not parallel the verb phrase "confirming eligibility," and the plural heading "Request Steps" is followed by only one malformed sentence rather than a list of steps.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two statements into a single owner and a single update schedule for the equipment catalog.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Program Overview section, which states the benefits team publishes the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month. The document gives two different owners and two different schedules for the same catalog.

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the repeated sentence or replace it with information specific to special cases.
findings.violation: This sentence is a verbatim repeat of a sentence already given in the Program Overview section and adds no new information in this context.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove the unrelated sentences, or if they are relevant, explain how they connect to the stipend program.
findings.violation: These three sentences have no stated connection to the home office equipment stipend and interrupt a section that is supposed to describe who coordinates stipend requests.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: State what action follows a flagged request, for example additional review, a hold on payment, or manager notification.
findings.violation: The document never says what happens after a request is flagged, so the consequence of the flag is undefined.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match its content, for example "Vendor List Updates," and clarify how the vendor list relates to the other two documents already introduced.
findings.violation: The heading "Questions and Updates" promises questions, but the section contains none, only a publishing statement. It also reuses the exact "most recent version supersedes" wording from Program Overview for a third document, the vendor list, without explaining how the vendor list relates to the equipment catalog or the reimbursement log.
